A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 26-page CompoDistill paper, including Appendices A-J. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical manuscript content, with only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp changing.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, attention analyses, ablations and scaling experiments in Sections 3, 5-6 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including CompoDistill evaluations and component, training-stage and scaling analyses.

M1.justification: The VAT attention-alignment module, group layer matching, TAF adapter and three-stage distillation procedure in Section 4 are identical, including their objectives and trainable components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VQA, compositional-reasoning and relational-hallucination benchmarks. The base training datasets and extended data mixture in Appendices E and G are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments, including LLaVA-KD, LLaVADI and LLaVA-MoD in Table 1, the hallucination comparisons, and the Simple/Adaptive layer-matching baselines.

E3.justification: Reported metrics, sampling procedures, model sizes, backbones, training budgets and data-scaling configurations are unchanged in Sections 3, 5-6 and Appendices E-H.

E4.justification: The same component, attention-loss, target-layer, matching-strategy and training-stage ablations appear in both versions. Attention interventions, qualitative examples and scaling analyses are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Neither the main text nor the appendices change uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are identical. For example, Table 1 reports CompoDistill-2B scores of 82.9 on SugarCrepe and 69.4 on SADE in both versions; appendix results are likewise unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention submatrices, group-matching formulation, adapter mapping and objectives in Equations 1-4 are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about visual attention misalignment, improved compositional reasoning, preserved VQA performance and generalization across backbones.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations of the experimental findings are identical. Appendix J retains the same limitations concerning attention-head averaging and vocabulary compatibility between teacher and student.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and training-data recipes in Appendices E-G are unchanged. No code/data resources or reproducibility access instructions are added or removed.

R1.justification: The references, Appendix I related-work discussion and Section 4.2 positioning relative to existing attention-distillation methods are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v1 dated 14 October 2025 to v2 dated 9 April 2026. Authors, title, manuscript wording, headings and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1-9 and Tables 1-17 retain identical contents, captions, styling and placement. There is no manuscript reflow or figure/table redesign; the margin-stamp text update is covered under P1.

improvement.justification: The methods, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information and limitations are identical across both PDFs, including all appendices. Updating only the arXiv version/date stamp creates no meaningful difference in paper quality.
